tools.chmod-calculator.metadata.title: Chmod Calculator
tools.chmod-calculator.metadata.descript: Calculate Unix file permissions visually using chmod
tools.chmod-calculator.faqs.0.question: What is chmod?
tools.chmod-calculator.faqs.0.answer: chmod is a command in Unix and Unix-like systems (such as Linux and macOS) used to change the permissions of files or directories. Permissions determine who can read, write or execute a file.
tools.chmod-calculator.faqs.1.question: How do permissions work?
tools.chmod-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Permissions are grouped into three classes: owner, group and others. Each class can have read (r, value 4), write (w, value 2) and execute (x, value 1) permissions. These values are added together to get the numeric representation (like 755).
tools.chmod-calculator.faqs.2.question: How do I use the chmod calculator?
tools.chmod-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Click the permission checkboxes to set the desired permissions for owner, group and others. The calculator shows the numeric and symbolic representations in real time.
tools.chmod-calculator.faqs.3.question: What is the difference between numeric and symbolic representations?
tools.chmod-calculator.faqs.3.answer: The numeric representation uses three digits (like 755), where each digit is the sum of the permission values. The symbolic representation uses letters (like rwxr-xr-x), where r means read, w means write, x means execute and - means no permission.
tools.chmod-calculator.faqs.4.question: What are common permission settings?
tools.chmod-calculator.faqs.4.answer: 755 (rwxr-xr-x) for directories and executable files, 644 (rw-r--r--) for regular files, 700 (rwx------) for private directories, and 600 (rw-------) for sensitive files.
tools.chmod-calculator.faqs.5.question: Can I set special permissions?
tools.chmod-calculator.faqs.5.answer: This calculator handles basic permissions. Special permissions (such as setuid, setgid and the sticky bit) require an additional fourth digit in the numeric representation.
tools.chmod-calculator.guide.intro.title: What is a Chmod Calculator?
tools.chmod-calculator.guide.intro.parag: A chmod calculator is a free online tool for calculating the numeric and symbolic representations of Unix file permissions. It helps you visualize permissions and generate the correct syntax for the chmod command. All calculations happen in the browser.
Click the permission checkboxes to set the desired permissions for owner, group and others. The calculator shows the numeric (like 755) and symbolic (like rwxr-xr-x) representations in real time.

tools.cron-generator.faqs.0.question: What is a cron expression?
tools.cron-generator.faqs.0.answer: A cron expression is a string used to schedule tasks on Unix-like systems. It consists of five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week. Each field can contain specific values, ranges, lists or wildcards.
tools.cron-generator.faqs.1.question: How do I build a cron expression?
tools.cron-generator.faqs.1.answer: Use the presets to quickly pick common schedules, or enter a value for each field manually. The tool shows the expression in English and displays the next run times.
tools.cron-generator.faqs.2.question: What are the fields of a cron expression?
tools.cron-generator.faqs.2.answer: A standard cron expression has five fields: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12) and day of week (0-7, where both 0 and 7 are Sunday).
tools.cron-generator.faqs.3.question: What does * mean in cron?
tools.cron-generator.faqs.3.answer: The asterisk (*) means "every" or "all". It matches every possible value for a field, meaning the task runs at every value of that field.
tools.cron-generator.faqs.4.question: How do I specify multiple values?
tools.cron-generator.faqs.4.answer: Use commas to separate values (like 1,3,5), hyphens for ranges (like 1-5), or step values (like */5 meaning every 5 units).
tools.cron-generator.faqs.5.question: Are cron expressions safe?
tools.cron-generator.faqs.5.answer: Yes. This tool generates cron expressions locally in the browser. No data is sent to any server.

tools.css-minifier.faqs.0.question: What is CSS minification?
tools.css-minifier.faqs.0.answer: CSS minification reduces the size of a CSS file by removing unnecessary whitespace, comments and other characters. This can improve page load speed and reduce bandwidth usage.
tools.css-minifier.faqs.1.question: How do I minify CSS?
tools.css-minifier.faqs.1.answer: Paste your CSS code into the input field. Click the minify button. The tool removes whitespace and comments to produce a smaller output. Copy the result or download the minified file.
tools.css-minifier.faqs.2.question: Does minification affect CSS functionality?
tools.css-minifier.faqs.2.answer: No. Minification only removes characters that are unnecessary for rendering. The functionality of your CSS remains unchanged. However, it may make the code harder to read or debug.
tools.css-minifier.faqs.3.question: How much can minification reduce file size?
tools.css-minifier.faqs.3.answer: The reduction depends on the original CSS. Files with lots of whitespace and comments can be reduced by 50-80%. Already compact CSS may see only a small reduction.
tools.css-minifier.faqs.4.question: Is my CSS sent to a server?
tools.css-minifier.faqs.4.answer: No. All minification happens locally in your browser. The code never leaves your device.
tools.css-minifier.faqs.5.question: Can I minify large CSS files?
tools.css-minifier.faqs.5.answer: Yes. Since minification happens in the browser, it can handle large CSS files. However, very large files (>50 MB) may be slow due to browser memory limits.

tools.favicon-generator.faqs.0.question: What is a favicon?
tools.favicon-generator.faqs.0.answer: A small icon displayed in the browser tab of a website.
tools.favicon-generator.faqs.1.question: How do I generate a favicon?
tools.favicon-generator.faqs.1.answer: Upload an image or pick an icon, adjust the size and generate your favicon.
tools.favicon-generator.faqs.2.question: Which formats are supported?
tools.favicon-generator.faqs.2.answer: ICO, PNG, SVG and more are supported.
tools.favicon-generator.faqs.3.question: Is the tool free?

tools.favicon-generator.guide.intro.para: A Favicon Generator is a free online tool that lets you generate favicons in multiple sizes from an image.
All processing happens in your browser — your data is never sent to a server.
tools.favicon-generator.guide.sections.0: Open the tool in your browser
Follow the instructions on the screen
Get your result and download it for use
tools.favicon-generator.guide.sections.1: Data is processed locally to protect your privacy
